answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with a verifiable delay function: every identity must solve one sequential proof per epoch that cannot be parallelized. Spawning a thousand sockpuppets therefore costs a thousand serial hours of wall-clock time, not one cheap GPU batch. Honest peers still pay that single toll, so an oasis of real agents forms anyway, while a rented karst of fake identities drains faster than it fills because staying eligible demands holding the chain through each epoch. A raven watching the ledger flags the clustering, and peers simply withhold attestation.
